resources.string: Course 3 · Advanced. 18 holes with branching fairways, central woodland and hills, narrow shortcuts between lakes and contoured greens. Build a par along the wide route or cut across with precision.

string-array.name: classic_wild_tips
string-array.item: Go around the wooded hill: wide left or tighter right with a better approach angle.
The broad right crescent builds a prudent par 5. The left shortcut is a 17 m ribbon between two lakes.
Carry the water without running into the rear sand. The right apron offers a bailout.
The high hill blocks the direct line. Use the wide left elbow or the shorter right saddle.
From the high tee, attack the green across the lake or set up an approach on the right terrace.
Follow the wide right bank or hop between the small left landings: water fills the gaps.
The high right apron feeds towards the diagonal green. Short shots find sand.
Two fairways skirt the huge central bunker. Left is wide; right demands a placed drive.
The broad right S avoids the pines; the left route is shorter with little room to miss.
The descent adds distance. Choose the broad right bank or the small left landing beside the lake.
Two routes encircle the wooded hill. The broad left detour offers space; the right route shortens the approach.
Control carry between front water and rear sand. The right apron avoids the narrowest target.
Three routes: wide left, short right, or a 17 m ribbon between the two central bunkers.
Skirt the wooded ridge on either balcony. The green climbs: take enough club to reach the terrace.
Cut across either cape over water. The bank routes remain playable with several placed shots.
Place a long iron between lake and sand; the front-left apron sets up a conservative chip.
The left shelf is wide but leaves a diagonal approach. The right lane hugs water and opens the green.
Final par 5: build along the broad right crescent or brave the 18 m causeway between the lakes.
